title: Aaron Sorkin on Hollywood’s Vision of American Politics
excerpt: On The Political Scene Podcast, The Oscar-winning writer of “The Social Network” and creator of “The West Wing” joins Tyler Foggatt live onstage at The New Yorker Festival.
content_html:
The Oscar-winning writer of “The Social Network” and creator of “The West Wing” joins Tyler Foggatt live onstage at The New Yorker Festival.

November 25, 2026

Listen and subscribe: Apple | Spotify | Wherever You Listen

Sign up to receive our twice-weekly News & Politics newsletter.

The screenwriter, playwright, and director Aaron Sorkin joins Tyler Foggatt for a live conversation at the annual New Yorker Festival to reflect on his work and career writing about politics for the screen. He discusses his approach to creating characters and writing dialogue, the enduring influence of “The West Wing,” and the show’s idealistic portrayal of American politics. He also discusses Trump-era nostalgia for an imagined past, the origins of his new film, “The Social Reckoning,” and the ways that social media has reshaped public discourse.

This conversation was recorded live at Webster Hall on October 25th, during the annual New Yorker Festival.

Tune in to The Political Scene wherever you get your podcasts.

  • What happened when an N.B.A. player got hooked on sports betting and in debt to the wrong people.

  • “That winter I continued to exercise a lot, hoping to become thin and muscular enough for him to fall in love with me.”

  • The Odyssey cruise was supposed to last a lifetime. Instead, it became a floating fiasco.
